Hi Marissa / Rishi,

Thanks for the quick kickoff today. As we discussed, the execs want a firm recommendation by next Friday on whether we should proceed with Redwood in a VPC-hosted configuration or push for an on-prem appliance pilot. The key constraints from our side:

- Regulatory: any PII must never leave our controlled environment without tokenization.
- Retention: legal wants configurable retention windows (30/90/365 days) + explicit delete proofs.
- KMS/HSM: must integrate with our key management (Azure Key Vault).

Can your team confirm the following for the MAP so we can lock timelines:
1) Feasibility of VPC with customer-managed KMS and a mirrored on-prem evaluation.
2) What artifact/evidence you can provide for deletion/audit logs (SOC2 snapshot ok?).
3) Proposed owners and a cadence for MAP checkpoints (we prefer weekly).

Appreciate a short plan and owners.

Best,
Tom
Senior Product Ops, Fintegrate

Marissa / team — brief security readout and constraints from our side: please see notes below. Happy to review live on Wed.

High-level constraints for on-prem vs VPC:
- VPC-hosted (customer VPC peering or private link): quickest path to production. We support customer-managed KMS (AWS/ Azure/ GCP) but need an integration window of ~2 weeks to validate key rotation and access patterns.
- On-prem appliance: feasible but requires an air-gapped checklist (network egress controls, packaging, dependency list). Hardware sizing and installation are typically +4 weeks for an initial pilot.

PII and retention specifics:
- Tokenization at ingress is preferred for regulated fields (SSNs, payment PANs). We can offer per-field pseudonymization but that increases latency and will need evaluation.
- Audit logs: we can provide immutable event logs for delete requests and tokenization operations; format is JSON with timestamped events. We will produce a deletion audit report as part of the MAP deliverables.
- Retention controls: configurable retention policy is supported; we can map 30/90/365 day policies to buckets and provide automated purge runs with confirmation artifacts.

Required artifacts to move forward:
1) Fintegrate to share the list of sensitive fields and sample schema (sanitized) — Owner: Tom Reynolds
2) Confirmation of preferred KMS (Azure Key Vault noted in initial email) and POC for credentials exchange/testing — Owner: Fintegrate infra POC
3) SOC2-related artifact requests list (we will provide the snapshot and a one-pager on audit log formats) — Owner: Vivek (deliverable by 03/10)

Risks:
- If Fintegrate requires full on-prem delivery within 3 weeks, risk: hardware + compliance sign-off will likely push project by 4–6 weeks.
- Tokenization of live PII for evaluation requires strict staging controls; prefer using a sanitized dataset first.

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
